headline_marked: Actress Anjali Dinesh Anand [[takes roles for survival]] amid body-shaming controversy
headline: Actress Anjali Dinesh Anand takes roles for survival amid body-shaming controversy
summary: The actress responded to critics who questioned why she acted in a film that mocks weight, stating she must work to support her family.
details: Actress Anjali Dinesh Anand has sparked a debate after appearing in the movie 'Dhamaal 4', which contains several scenes that mock a character's weight.
Content creator Soumya Dubey criticized the actress, questioning how someone who advocates for body positivity can participate in a film that reinforces negative stereotypes.
Anjali responded by explaining the gap between her ideals and the reality of her professional life, stating that she does not have the luxury of choosing every role.
She stated that she must take the roles offered to her to support her family and buy food, describing the process as 'swallowing bitter medicine'.
The actress emphasized that acting a role does not mean she supports the behavior of the character, comparing it to an actor playing a serial killer without supporting murder.
Anjali expressed hope that the industry's perspective on plus-size actors will change over time and that she is prepared to wait for that shift.
She urged the public to judge her based on her talent and acting skills rather than her body size.
Anjali has previously appeared in projects such as 'Dhai Kilo Prem', 'Untagged', and 'Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani'.
caption:
“I have to run my household, I have to buy food.”

Actress Anjali Dinesh Anand opens up about taking roles that contradict her beliefs for survival.

Actress Anjali Dinesh Anand has sparked a debate after appearing in the movie 'Dhamaal 4', which contains several scenes that mock a character's weight.

Content creator Soumya Dubey criticized the actress, questioning how someone who advocates for body positivity can participate in a film that reinforces negative stereotypes.

Anjali responded by explaining the gap between her ideals and the reality of her professional life, stating that she does not have the luxury of choosing every role.

She stated that she must take the roles offered to her to support her family and buy food, describing the process as 'swallowing bitter medicine'.

The actress emphasized that acting a role does not mean she supports the behavior of the character, comparing it to an actor playing a serial killer without supporting murder.

Anjali expressed hope that the industry's perspective on plus-size actors will change over time and that she is prepared to wait for that shift.

She urged the public to judge her based on her talent and acting skills rather than her body size.

Anjali has previously appeared in projects such as 'Dhai Kilo Prem', 'Untagged', and 'Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani'.

headline: 62% faster decline: Artificial sweeteners may harm brain health
summary: A new study published in Neurology suggests a link between high consumption of sugar substitutes and faster decline in memory and cognitive abilities.
details: A study published in the journal Neurology by the American Academy of Neurology shows that people who regularly consume high amounts of artificial sweeteners may experience a faster decline in memory and mental capacity.
Researchers observed approximately 12,772 adults in Brazil over eight years, with an average age of 52. Participants were divided into three groups based on their intake of sugar substitutes.

The findings revealed that those with the highest intake of artificial sweeteners saw their memory and cognitive functions decline approximately 62% faster than those with the lowest intake. This difference is equivalent to the brain aging by about 1.6 years.

The study included seven common sweeteners: aspartame, saccharin, acesulfame-K, erythritol, xylitol, sorbitol, and tagatose. These are typically found in diet sodas, energy drinks, low-calorie desserts, and processed foods.
The risk was more pronounced in people under 60 and those with diabetes. Six out of the seven sweeteners studied showed a link to memory loss, while tagatose did not show such a relationship.

Researchers cautioned that this is an observational study and does not prove a direct cause-and-effect relationship. They noted that participants provided their own dietary information, which could lead to inaccuracies.

Health experts advise against relying excessively on artificial sweeteners and suggest maintaining a balanced, natural diet. They emphasize that 'sugar-free' does not mean these products can be consumed without limit.
